technical_and_design_decisions: Extend the existing Spring XD configuration and module mechanisms rather than introducing a separate configuration subsystem.
Represent Docker container environment variables and external-service bindings as declarative configuration, with generated container settings remaining backward compatible.

Implement service discovery behind a provider-neutral abstraction so the container configuration is not tightly coupled to one discovery product; use the existing deployment/runtime integration where available.
Create Docker images reproducibly through CI using versioned Dockerfiles, build scripts, automated tests, and a configurable image registry destination.
Use the existing Spring XD partitioned-job abstractions for configurable RDBMS-to-HDFS partitioning, preserving current behavior when no strategy is supplied.
Implement HDFS ingestion as a standard Spring XD source module using the existing module lifecycle, configuration, and message transport conventions.
Expose commit interval as an optional servers.yml setting, with the current default retained when the setting is absent and applied to all supported out-of-the-box partitioned jobs.
Evaluate Spring Boot upgrades incrementally using dependency reports, compatibility analysis, regression tests, and documented upgrade recommendations.
Treat Mesos and Marathon deployment guidance as operational documentation based on the supported XD cluster topology, networking, persistence, scaling, and health-check requirements.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD source code, build system, test framework, module APIs, and deployment configuration are available and buildable.
The increment is implemented by one developer; estimates represent hands-on workdays and exclude elapsed calendar time, waiting for environments, and unrelated maintenance.

The specification does not identify exact service-discovery products, so the implementation will integrate with the existing project conventions or provide a minimal provider-neutral extension rather than support every discovery system.
Docker, a CI service, a Docker image registry, HDFS, Mesos, Marathon, and representative external services are available for testing or can be represented with local test doubles.
Docker support is limited to configuration, image creation, and integration hooks; it does not include implementing or operating a complete container orchestration platform.
Existing out-of-the-box partitioned jobs and their current commit-interval behavior can be identified without redesigning their processing algorithms.
Backward compatibility is required for existing configurations, modules, jobs, and deployments unless explicitly changed by the new options.
The Spring Boot upgrade evaluation covers a bounded target upgrade selected from currently compatible releases and does not include a full migration to a different Spring major version.
Documentation will cover recommendations and examples, not a production deployment or performance certification.
Code review, release packaging, and final regression verification are included in the estimates, while external approval cycles are excluded.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing Spring XD container, module, job, configuration, build, and deployment code; map each user story to extension points; define compatibility and test strategy.

Implement configuration and rendering of Docker linking or binding attributes and environment variables, including validation, defaults, representative service examples, unit tests, and integration tests.

Add service-discovery configuration and runtime integration for XD containers, including discovery settings, provider integration points, failure handling, backward-compatible defaults, and automated tests.
Create or update Dockerfiles, build scripts, CI jobs, image tagging and publishing configuration, build-time configuration handling, and automated smoke tests for produced images.

Produce and validate deployment documentation covering cluster topology, Marathon application configuration, resource sizing, networking, persistence, scaling, health checks, upgrades, and operational caveats.

Select and apply the target dependency upgrade in an evaluation branch, inspect transitive changes, resolve build or API issues, execute regression tests, and document compatibility risks and recommendations.
Add the partitioning-strategy configuration model and validation, connect it to RDBMS ingest partition planning and job creation, preserve the default strategy, and add unit and integration coverage.

Implement the HDFS source module, including path and file-selection configuration, input reading, message conversion, error handling, lifecycle behavior, module metadata, and representative HDFS or test-double integration tests.
Add the optional servers.yml commit-interval property, propagate it to every supported out-of-the-box partitioned job, retain the existing default, validate values, and add regression tests.
Run the complete build and test suite, exercise Docker and ingest scenarios together, verify configuration backward compatibility, diagnose failures, and fix defects found during integration.
Update configuration and module reference documentation, add usage examples and release notes, clean build and CI artifacts, perform final review, and prepare the increment for delivery.
